objective: Prepare the exact thermofield-double (TFD) state of the certified sparse-SYK instances Row 42 (primary), Rows 48/32/30, and Eq. 11 (baseline) from campaign syk-gist-routed-instance, at beta=3, with as high a fidelity as possible under a hard two-qubit-gate budget. The candidate emits, per instance, a gate-level circuit (never a statevector); the scorer simulates that circuit itself on the 8-qubit (256-dimensional) doubled register starting from |0>^8 (every candidate prepares its own reference: the 35-CNOT baseline via 8 Hadamards to |+>^8, a ma-QAOA candidate via its own |I> prep), computes the fidelity against the sealed exact TFD, and counts the circuit's logical two-qubit cost. The scientific target is the fidelity-vs-cost curve of ma-QAOA + sequential angle pruning (SAP/OSAP, arXiv:2609.02793 Algorithms 1 and 2) against the fixed 35-CNOT hardware-efficient block at matched cost. CONVENTION FLAG for the reply: the 35-CNOT block's fidelity F35 is measured |0>->TFD; ma-QAOA's native reference is |I> (their Eq. 18). |I> factorizes as a Bell pair on qubits (0,1) tensor |0> on qubits 2..7, so its prep is ONE CX (provided, verified, as reference_prep_gates). The logical cost axis counts the full |0>->TFD circuit (device-honest); the memo also reports the QAOA-layers-only sub-count (their convention, where |I> is a free reference).
metric_definition: LOWER IS BETTER, and it is now MECHANISM-DISCRIMINATING (revised 2026-09-21 after the first run shipped a mere 35-CNOT-block re-fit). The five certified instances and their exact beta=3 targets, |I>, verified |0>^8->|I> prep, H_cost/H_mix Pauli strings, and sealed F35 are loaded from tfd_targets.npz (built by seal_targets.py reusing the sibling verifier's convention verbatim; see prior contract text). Per instance the scorer loads the sealed target and F35, calls candidate.prepare(payload) (payload carries terms/signs/Jc/jw_map/beta/|I>/reference_prep_gates/H_cost/H_mix/H_L, NEVER the target), simulates the returned circuit from |0>^8, and recomputes F = |<target|psi>|^2 and the logical two-qubit cost C2 (cx/cz=1, rzz/rxx/ryy=2). The per-instance score REWARDS CHEAP PREPARATION AT OR ABOVE THE ANCHOR FIDELITY: s_i = 1000*max(0, F35_i - F_i) + C2_i. The 1000x weight on any fidelity debt below F35 means cost can never be bought by sacrificing fidelity; once F_i >= F35_i the score is just the two-qubit cost, so the objective is the minimum cost that still reaches the anchor fidelity. A fixed 35-CNOT block (cost exactly 35 by construction) can only ever score ~35 here, so reproducing the block is NOT a win; a win requires a genuinely cheaper prep (e.g. ma-QAOA + SAP/OSAP pruning) that keeps F >= F35. score = mean_i s_i. Nothing the candidate reports is read. C2 above 70 is INVALID (blocks exact-state synthesis). The routed axis (A35, FakeMarrakesh best-of-11) is bound at the freeze gate; this scorer gates on the deterministic logical axis and the sealed per-instance F35 (0.8955 Row 42, 0.9164 Row 48, 0.9011 Row 32, 0.9228 Row 30, 0.9229 Eq. 11). The scientific object is the fidelity-vs-cost tradeoff of ma-QAOA pruning vs the fixed 35-CNOT block; the scored quantity is the crossing point (cheapest prep reaching F35), and an honest null (pruning cannot reach F35 below 35 gates at beta=3) is an equally shippable result.
promotion_bar: A candidate is promoted when the blinded scorer returns a strictly lower score than the incumbent by at least min_improvement, with valid=true on all five instances. Because the score is now 1000*max(0,F35-F)+C2 per instance, a lower score means either reaching F35 on more instances or reaching it at LOWER two-qubit cost. Reproducing the 35-CNOT block (F35 at cost 35) scores ~35 and cannot beat an incumbent already at ~35; only genuinely cheaper F35-reaching preparation promotes. Stochastic wins require independent fresh-seed confirmation; wins >= 25% force an adversarial audit.
kill_criteria: REACHABILITY KILL: the un-pruned ma-QAOA ansatz cannot reach F >= 0.9999 on the primary instance by p=8 with the pre-registered initial-fit budget (5 random inits per p from default_rng(100+p), L-BFGS-B with analytic gradients, maxiter 3000, ftol 0, gtol 1e-10). Ships as a certified negative with the reached F(p) table for p=3..8.

MATCHED-COST NULL (higher refutation bar): on all five instances both SAP and OSAP give F < F35(instance) - 0.02 at every cost C2 <= 35, in BOTH the algorithm-exact column (warm start from current angles, box current +/- pi, maxiter 300, no random re-inits inside the loop) and the labeled post-hoc polish column (6 inits from default_rng(1000+point_index) x 800 iterations on the frozen pruned structure, never fed back into block selection). Ships as QUESTION-STATUS with the crossing cost on both axes. A polished-only crossing is not a null and not a clean win: it ships as the labeled 'structure wins, their reoptimizer does not' outcome.

SCORER INTEGRITY: every scored quantity is recomputed by the scorer from the candidate's gate list; the candidate's own reported fidelities and counts are discarded. At the verifier-freeze gate the sealed verifier must additionally pass, all as tolerance-gated deterministic forward computations with no optimizer and no hash gate on recomputed floats: (i-a) sha256 of workspace/tfd_targets.npz verified and each recomputed gauge-fixed target within 1e-9 elementwise of the stored vector (rounded-vector hashes are reported provenance only); (i-b) each sealed F35(instance) reproduced from its stored 6x8x2 angle array to 1e-9 after the array sha256 check; (i-c) seed-0 block fidelity computed and reported ungated; (ii) the sibling full-protocol routed_cost() on Eq. 11 with the pinned block reproduced as 314 best-of-11 to 0 gates; (iii) A35 stable across two independent runs. Any failure kills the cycle until fixed.

BASELINE FAIRNESS HOLD: the sealed baseline refit runs BASELINE_FIT_SEED=0, 6 inits x 3000 L-BFGS-B iterations with the candidates' own ftol 0 / gtol 1e-10, recording every init's status, termination message, nit, nfev and final gradient infinity-norm; one pre-registered continuation if the winner stops on maxiter with gradient norm above 1e-6; one pre-registered escalation (12 inits from default_rng(1), same settings) if F35 lands more than 0.005 BELOW the sibling JSON floor. Still more than 0.005 below after the escalation: the discover round HOLDS for the Director before freeze.
BUDGET: more than 3 subscription windows or more than 2 verifier redraft rounds before the first certified primary-instance curve; park and hand the current state to the Director.
ship_condition: All five instances reach F >= F35(instance) at a logical two-qubit cost STRICTLY BELOW 35 (the pruned prep is genuinely cheaper than the fixed 35-CNOT block at matched-or-better fidelity), i.e. mean score <= 33.0 with every instance at F >= F35 and C2 < 35, with the full fidelity-vs-cost curve (SAP and OSAP) recorded per instance. The certified matched-cost NULL (ma-QAOA + pruning cannot reach F35 below 35 gates at beta=3 on these instances) is an equally shippable terminal state and ships as QUESTION-STATUS with the crossing cost on both the logical and routed axes.

reduction.source_type: Physics existence/quantitative question: does an angle-pruned, Hamiltonian-structured variational ansatz prepare the beta=3 SYK thermofield double at higher fidelity per two-qubit gate than a fixed hardware-efficient block?
reduction.target_type: optimization (search over circuit structure and angles, verified by exact simulation)
reduction.transform: The question becomes: emit a gate-level circuit on an 8-qubit doubled register whose simulated output from |I> overlaps the exactly computed TFD. PRESERVED: the exact 256-dimensional state, the exact Hamiltonian, the fidelity definition, and a hard gate-cost budget, so the fidelity-vs-cost tradeoff is the scored object rather than a proxy. LOST at this stage: the routed (transpiled, hardware-connectivity) cost axis C1 and one-qubit gate counts, which are reported at the verifier-freeze gate and are not gated here; also lost is any hardware noise model (this is a noiseless rung-2 oracle), so the result is an upper bound on what hardware would show.
reduction.signal: Continuous and decomposed. (a) Primary gradient: 100*(1 - F) per instance is smooth in the ansatz angles, so every optimizer step moves the score. (b) Per-instance decomposition: the score averages five independently reported instances, so progress on a subset is visible even when others stall. (c) Cost checkpoint: a separate additive term 100*max(0, (C2-35)/35) makes each removed two-qubit gate above the cap visible before the cap is reached, giving pruning its own gradient. (d) The scorer's reason string reports per instance F, C2, and whether the 0.887 bar is crossed, so a candidate can be at score 90 (untuned block), 40 (fit but over budget), 12 (pruned to budget, near the bar) or below 11.3 (ship) with a continuum between.
reduction.completeness: Solving the target answers the source for the scored instance family up to two stated gaps: (1) the routed-cost axis is not gated at this stage, so a circuit that wins on logical CNOTs might not win after transpilation to FakeMarrakesh connectivity; the freeze-gate verifier closes this by routing both ansatz families through one pipeline. (2) The fidelity bar is provisionally the sibling JSON floor rather than the sealed budget-matched refit F35(instance); a win margin below 0.02 is therefore not claimable until the sealed anchors replace the floor. Both gaps are anchored, not open-ended: neither can flip a certified null, and both can only tighten a claimed win.

dev_examples:
The candidate module must define prepare(payload) -> dict. Payload per instance (read-only; the exact TFD target is NEVER included):

  payload = {
    'name': 'INST-A',            # INST-A..E = Row 42/48/32/30, Eq. 11
    'beta': 3.0,
    'n_qubits': 8,               # doubled register (GIST Eq. 5: psi_L, psi_R share these 8 qubits)
    'K': 12, 'Jc': 0.4082,       # number of four-body terms; coupling scale sqrt(2)/sqrt(K)
    'terms': [[1,2,5,6], ...],   # K quartets over Majoranas 1..8 (one-indexed, sibling convention)
    'signs': [-1, ...],          # +/-1 per term (binary sparse)
    'jw_map': [5,4,7,3,6,8],      # the instance's pair-to-qubit map (their Eq. S2)
    'reference_state': ndarray(256,) complex,      # |I>, the ma-QAOA reference (H_int ground state)
    'reference_prep_gates': [{'name':'x','qubits':[1],'param':0.0}, ...],  # VERIFIED |0>^8 -> |I>
                                 # (1 CX; |I>=(|01>+i|10>)/sqrt2 on q0,q1 tensor |0> on q2..7). Prepend
                                 # this if your ansatz starts from |I>; do not re-derive it.
    'h_cost': [('IIZXIIYZ',(0.10+0j)), ...],   # H_cost = H_L + H_R as (8-char Pauli label, coeff), 2K strings
    'h_mix':  [('ZIIIIIII',(-0.5+0j)), ...],   # H_mix = H_int as (label, coeff), N=8 single-qubit-Z strings
    'h_left': ndarray(256,256) complex,        # dense single-side-in-doubled-space H_L (default map)
  }

Return the FULL circuit from |0>^8 to the prepared state (prepare your own reference: 8 H for the hardware-efficient block, or reference_prep_gates for ma-QAOA):

  {'n_qubits': 8, 'gates': [{'name':'h','qubits':[0],'param':0.0}, {'name':'cx','qubits':[0,1],'param':0.0}, {'name':'rzz','qubits':[2,6],'param':-1.1}]}

Supported gates: 1q h,x,y,z,s,sdg,rx,ry,rz; 2q cx (first qubit = control), cz, rzz, rxx, ryy. Rotations use exp(-i*theta*P/2). Logical 2q cost: cx/cz=1, rzz/rxx/ryy=2. Limits: <=5000 gates; cost>70 INVALID; cost>35 penalized. Simulated from |0>^8 (qubit 0 most significant, matching the sealed |I>, target and Pauli labels: leftmost label char = qubit 0). Build ma-QAOA cost/mixer evolutions directly from h_cost/h_mix (each e^{-i theta P/2} = CNOT-ladder + Rz over the support of P). Nothing besides the gate list is read.

PERFORMANCE & DETERMINISM: the scorer runs the 5 instances IN PARALLEL (one forked process each) and its workers are non-daemonic, so prepare() MAY use multiprocessing (fork context) with up to 2 worker processes to parallelize independent work (ma-QAOA restarts, OSAP N_C candidate reoptimizations). REQUIRED: key every RNG seed on payload['name'] (e.g. a hash of it), NEVER on call order, a module-global counter, or wall-clock time, and use a FIXED iteration budget (no wall-clock deadline). This makes the score deterministic and the five instances exchangeable, so results do not depend on scheduling or machine load.
